faqs.q: What are carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets used for?
faqs.a: Carbon steel and clad tube sheets hold the tubes of shell-and-tube exchangers, feedwater heaters and condensers, in SA-516-70 plate or SA-266, SA-105, SA-350 LF2 and SA-182 forgings. They are plain or explosion-clad or overlaid, and finished to your drawing and TEMA.

faqs.q: How do I order the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets when there is no size table?
faqs.a: The Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets are made to your drawing, so there is no catalogue part number for each size. Send the drawing, or the material, the outside diameter, the thickness, the tube size and the pitch and layout, and we quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

faqs.q: What is the minimum tube pitch for the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: For the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets, the minimum tube pitch is 1.25 × tube OD, triangular or square: 19.84 mm for 15.88 mm (5/8 in) tube, 23.81 mm for 19.05 mm (3/4 in) and 31.75 mm for 25.40 mm (1 in) tube. These are the limits of the standard, not part numbers.

faqs.q: How thick is the explosion-clad layer on a tube sheet?
faqs.a: The explosion-clad layer is typically 3–10 mm for tube sheets, with 1–50 mm possible and a base of 10–500 mm, single pieces to about 50 t, and flatness within 1 mm/m.

faqs.q: What are the tube hole and expansion details for the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: For a standard 3/4 in (19.05 mm) tube the nominal hole is 0.760 in (19.30 mm), and for 1 in (25.4 mm) tube 1.012 in (25.70 mm), both with a 0.004 in (0.10 mm) under-tolerance. Holes are drilled and reamed 0.007–0.010 in (0.18–0.25 mm) over tube OD, with 1 groove when the sheet is 25 mm or thinner and 2 grooves when thicker.

faqs.q: Which materials are the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets made from?
faqs.a: Base material is SA-516-70 plate for thinner sheets and forged discs (SA-266, SA-105, SA-350 LF2, SA-182) above about 100–125 mm or for high-integrity service; SA-350 LF2 is used for low-temperature service. Cladding is explosion-clad (SS 304L/316L, duplex 2205/2507, Ti Gr1/2, alloy 625/825/C-276, Cu-Ni 90/10 or 70/30) or weld overlay.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: The sheets are listed to TEMA (10th ed. / 2026 ed.), ASME VIII Div 1 (Part UHX) and ASTM A516, A266, A105, A350, A182, A240, A263, A264 and A265, with API 660 / API 661 and EN 13445-3. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request.

faqs.q: What goes with the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets in an exchanger?
faqs.a: Tube sheets are drilled and grooved for the tubes and used with [baffles and tube supports](/c/baffles-tube-supports) and [forged flanges for exchangers](/c/forged-flanges-exchangers); the [tube sheets shelf](/c/tube-sheets) lists the other materials. Square-pitch tube sheets use a cleaning lane of at least 6.4 mm (1/4 in) for mechanical cleaning. [Our tube sheet drilling, pitch and baffle hole guide](/blog/tube-sheet-drilling-pitch-baffle-holes) covers drilling, pitch and baffle holes.

faqs.q: What testing applies to the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: Clad bond is tested by 100% UT per ASME SA-263 / SA-264 / SA-265, including after simulated PWHT. The completed exchanger is hydrotested, and tube-to-tubesheet procedure qualification needs purchaser approval under API 661.

faqs.q: How do the Carbon Steel and Clad Tube Sheets compare with other tube sheet materials?
faqs.a: Compared with solid alloy sheets, carbon steel with explosion cladding keeps full alloy chemistry (no dilution) and the full clad thickness is drillable and weldable, while weld overlay adds dilution, heat input and distortion and suits small or one-off parts. For solid alloys see the [Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets](/p/duplex-stainless-tube-sheets) and [Titanium Tube Sheets](/p/titanium-tube-sheets).

faqs.q: What are duplex Stainless Tube Sheets used for?
faqs.a: Duplex stainless tube sheets in F51 (S31803) and super duplex F53 (S32750), solid or clad on carbon steel, hold the tubes of seawater coolers and exchangers in chloride service. Typical uses are desalination and produced-water service and seawater-cooled exchangers in gas plants and refineries.

faqs.q: How do I order the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets when there is no size table?
faqs.a: The Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets are made to your drawing, so there is no catalogue part number for each size. Send the drawing, or the material, the outside diameter, the thickness, the tube size and the pitch and layout, and we quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

faqs.q: What is the minimum tube pitch for the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: For the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets, the minimum tube pitch is 1.25 × tube OD, triangular or square: 19.84 mm for 15.88 mm (5/8 in) tube, 23.81 mm for 19.05 mm (3/4 in) and 31.75 mm for 25.40 mm (1 in) tube. These are the limits of the standard, not part numbers.

faqs.q: What clad options exist for duplex tube sheets?
faqs.a: Duplex 2205 or super duplex 2507 can be explosion-clad on SA-516-70 or P355GH as an alternative to solid F51 or F53, used for seawater coolers and chloride streams.

faqs.q: What are the tube hole and expansion details for the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: A special close fit of the holes is mandatory in air-cooled exchanger headers when duplex tubes are used (API 661 / ISO 13706 cl. 9.3.1.2). Expansion is a 4–5% wall reduction with minimal re-rolling because of work hardening, and holes are drilled, reamed and then sized or burnished with no longitudinal scoring.

faqs.q: Which materials are the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets made from?
faqs.a: Grades are SA/A182 F51 (UNS S31803) duplex and F53 (UNS S32750) super duplex, with SA-240 plate equivalents; the clad alternative is duplex 2205 or super duplex 2507 explosion-clad on SA-516-70 or P355GH.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: The sheets are listed to ASTM A182 / ASME SA-182 F51 and F53, ASTM A240 S31803 / S32750, TEMA and NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged.

faqs.q: What goes with the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets in an exchanger?
faqs.a: Tube sheets are drilled and grooved for the tubes and used with [baffles and tube supports](/c/baffles-tube-supports) and [forged flanges for exchangers](/c/forged-flanges-exchangers); the [tube sheets shelf](/c/tube-sheets) lists the other materials. [Our tube sheet drilling, pitch and baffle hole guide](/blog/tube-sheet-drilling-pitch-baffle-holes) covers drilling, pitch and baffle holes.

faqs.q: What testing applies to the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: Bond UT is done if the sheet is clad, and ferrite and microstructure checks are per the purchaser specification. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request.

faqs.q: How do the Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets compare with other tube sheet materials?
faqs.a: Duplex and super duplex suit chloride service where carbon steel with cladding would be overlaid, while the [Titanium Tube Sheets](/p/titanium-tube-sheets) suit seawater condensers and the [Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets](/p/naval-brass-and-copper-alloy-tube-sheets) suit copper-alloy tubes. Choose by the tube material and the chloride duty.

faqs.q: What are naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets used for?
faqs.a: Naval brass and copper-alloy tube sheets in C46400 and other copper alloys to ASTM B171 hold the tubes of condensers and coolers with copper-alloy tubes. They are typically matched to Cu-Ni or Al-brass tubes in seawater condensers and coolers.

faqs.q: How do I order the Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets when there is no size table?
faqs.a: The Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets are made to your drawing, so there is no catalogue part number for each size. faqs.q: What is the minimum tube pitch for the Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: The Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets cover plate up to 140 mm (5 in) thick in tempers M20 (as hot rolled) and O25 (hot rolled and annealed; O25 only for the ASME Code). The listing gives thickness bands and minimum strength by alloy, and the size and pitch come from your drawing.

faqs.q: What strength do naval brass tube sheets have?
faqs.a: C46400 / C46500 naval brass lists a minimum tensile of 345 MPa, a yield of 140 MPa and 35 % elongation up to 80 mm plate, and 125 MPa yield from 80 to 140 mm. Other alloys list their own figures in the listing.

faqs.q: What are the tube hole and expansion details for the Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: Plate thickness tolerance for 25–38 mm plate up to 1000 mm wide is ±0.97 mm (Cu-Ni +25%). The listing gives minimum tensile, yield and elongation by alloy and thickness, such as C46400 naval brass at 345 MPa tensile and 35 % elongation up to 80 mm.

faqs.q: Which materials are the Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets made from?
faqs.a: Naval brass C46400 is Cu 59.0–62.0, Sn 0.5–1.0, Pb up to 0.20, Fe up to 0.10 and the rest Zn, in tempers M20 (as hot rolled) and O25 (hot rolled and annealed), up to 140 mm thick. Other alloys covered are admiralty, 90-10 and 70-30 Cu-Ni and aluminium bronze.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: The sheets are listed to ASTM B171/B171M and B122/B122M, DIN EN1653, GB/T 2040 and JIS H3100, with a tension test per E8. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged.

faqs.q: What are titanium Tube Sheets used for?
faqs.a: Titanium tube sheets in Grades 1 and 2, solid (ASTM B265 plate, B381 forgings) or explosion-clad on carbon steel, hold the tubes of seawater condensers and desalination plants. They also serve seawater coolers on offshore and coastal gas facilities.

faqs.q: How do I order the Titanium Tube Sheets when there is no size table?
faqs.a: The Titanium Tube Sheets are made to your drawing, so there is no catalogue part number for each size. Send the drawing, or the material, the outside diameter, the thickness, the tube size and the pitch and layout, and we quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

faqs.q: What is the minimum tube pitch for the Titanium Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: For the Titanium Tube Sheets, the minimum tube pitch is 1.25 × tube OD, triangular or square: 19.84 mm for 15.88 mm (5/8 in) tube, 23.81 mm for 19.05 mm (3/4 in) and 31.75 mm for 25.40 mm (1 in) tube. These are the limits of the standard, not part numbers.

faqs.q: How strong is the bond on explosion-clad titanium tube sheets?
faqs.a: Typical titanium-steel bond strength is 35,000–45,000 psi shear, with a backer plate usually at least 3/4 in (19 mm) thick. ASTM B898 requires a minimum of 20,000 psi (137.9 MPa) when Supplementary Requirement S1 is specified.

faqs.q: What are the tube hole and expansion details for the Titanium Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: A special close fit of the holes is mandatory with titanium tubes in API 661 headers. Expansion is a 4–5% wall reduction, and expanders with 4 or more rolls limit tube-end cracking.

faqs.q: Which materials are the Titanium Tube Sheets made from?
faqs.a: Grades are ASTM B265 plate Gr 1 / Gr 2 and ASTM B381 forgings F-1 / F-2, or titanium Gr 1/2 explosion-clad on SA-516-70 for seawater condensers, desalination, PTA and chlor-alkali. Bonnet headers are used where the tubesheet is an expensive alloy such as titanium.

faqs.q: Which standards and certificates apply to the Titanium Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: The sheets are listed to ASTM B265 / ASME SB-265, ASTM B381 / ASME SB-381, ASTM B898 and ISO 2768-fH. A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request, and third-party inspection can be arranged.

faqs.q: What goes with the Titanium Tube Sheets in an exchanger?
faqs.a: Tube sheets are drilled and grooved for the tubes and used with [baffles and tube supports](/c/baffles-tube-supports) and [forged flanges for exchangers](/c/forged-flanges-exchangers); the [tube sheets shelf](/c/tube-sheets) lists the other materials. [Our tube sheet drilling, pitch and baffle hole guide](/blog/tube-sheet-drilling-pitch-baffle-holes) covers drilling, pitch and baffle holes.

faqs.q: What testing applies to the Titanium Tube Sheets?
faqs.a: Bond is tested by UT, and the clad bond shear test (B898 S1) is done only if specified, with a minimum of 20,000 psi (137.9 MPa). A mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 is available on request.

faqs.q: How do the Titanium Tube Sheets compare with other tube sheet materials?
faqs.a: Titanium suits seawater condensers and desalination, while the [Duplex Stainless Tube Sheets](/p/duplex-stainless-tube-sheets) suit chloride service in gas plants and refineries and the [Naval Brass and Copper-Alloy Tube Sheets](/p/naval-brass-and-copper-alloy-tube-sheets) match copper-alloy tubes. Clad titanium on carbon steel gives titanium surface at lower cost than a solid sheet.
